name: Hidradenitis Suppurativa

criteria.description: Typical recurrent, painful, deep-seated nodules or abscesses in characteristic locations
Lesions located in apocrine gland-bearing areas such as axillae, groin, and inframammary regions
Chronic or relapsing course with multiple episodes over at least 6 months
Presence of draining sinus tracts or scarring
Positive family history of hidradenitis suppurativa

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least two typical lesions in characteristic locations with chronicity of at least 6 months
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; biopsy is rarely required

pathognomonic.notes: Typically located in apocrine gland-bearing areas
Chronic lesions often develop interconnected sinus tracts
Result of repeated inflammation and healing

common.symptomName: Pain and tenderness at lesion sites
common.notes: Pain is often severe and impacts quality of life
Inflammation can cause swelling and redness

occasional.notes: Reactive enlargement of regional lymph nodes
May be related to chronic inflammation

rare.symptomName: Squamous cell carcinoma arising in chronic lesions

rare.notes: Secondary to chronic pain and social stigma

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) during flares
Anemia of chronic disease in prolonged cases
imaging: Ultrasound showing fluid collections and sinus tracts
MRI can delineate extent of deep tissue involvement
genetic: Mutations in gamma-secretase complex genes (e.g., NCSTN, PSEN1) in familial cases
other: Clinical diagnosis primarily based on history and physical exam
Histopathology shows follicular occlusion and perifolliculitis

redFlags: Non-healing ulcer with bleeding or atypical appearance
references: Garg A, et al. Hidradenitis Suppurativa: Epidemiology, Clinical Presentation, and Pathogenesis. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2020.

Alikhan A, et al. North American clinical management guidelines for hidradenitis suppurativa: A publication from the United States and Canadian Hidradenitis Suppurativa Foundations. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2019.
